issues.legal_issue: An application to a civil court under a special enactment, for which that enactment prescribes no limitation period, is governed by the residuary limitation rule.
material_facts: A statutory amendment allowed an applicant to seek a court direction if the designated officer failed to make a reference within the prescribed time.
The amendment prescribed no limitation period for applying to the court for that direction.
issues.conclusion: The residuary limitation rule applies to the application, requiring it to be made within three years from when the cause of action arises.
issues.legal_principle: Article 137 of the Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1963 applies to applications made to a civil court under special enactments when no other article expressly prescribes a limitation period. The Court relied on Kerala State Electricity Board, Trivandrum v. T.P.K.K. Amson & Besom, which held that Article 137 is not confined to applications under the Code of Civil Procedure. It noted that the High Court had followed Town Municipal Corporation, Athani v. Presiding Officer, Labour Court, Hubli, a decision that had been overruled; Nityanand M. Joshi v. L.I.C. of India had earlier cast doubt on the Athani decision.

predicates.special_law_application_to_civil_court: An applicant seeks relief from a civil court through a procedure created by a special enactment.
predicates.no_specific_limitation_period: The enactment provides no limitation period for making that application.

issues.definition: When an applicant seeks relief from a civil court under a special enactment that sets no time limit for the application, the residuary limitation rule applies.

issues.legal_issue: An application seeking a court direction for a reference is time-barred when it is filed more than three years after the cause of action to seek that direction arises.
material_facts: The claimants applied to the designated officer for a reference within the time allowed after service of the award.
The officer did not make the reference within the statutory period of 90 days after receiving the application.
The claimants applied to the civil court for a direction to make the reference more than five years after the award was served, and therefore more than three years after the 90-day period expired.
issues.conclusion: The application to the civil court was barred by limitation; the appeals were allowed, the High Court’s order was set aside, and the application was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 18(3)(a) and (b) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, as amended in the state, the officer had 90 days from receipt of the reference application to make the reference; upon expiry of that period without a reference, the cause of action to seek a court direction arose. Because Section 18(3)(b) prescribed no limitation period for that court application, Article 137 of the Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1963 required it to be made within three years of that cause of action.

predicates.reference_direction_proceeding: The proceeding is an application to a civil court seeking a direction that an officer make a statutory reference.
predicates.timely_reference_request: The claimant asked the officer to make the reference within the applicable period.
predicates.officer_failed_to_refer_within_allowed_t: The officer did not make the reference within the time allowed after receiving the claimant’s request.
predicates.court_application_more_than_three_years_: The claimant applied to the court more than three years after the officer’s failure caused the right to seek a court direction to arise.

issues.definition: A court application for a direction to make a reference is time-barred when the claimant made a timely reference request, the officer failed to refer within the allowed time, and the court application came more than three years after the resulting cause of action arose.
